nodes.label: Contributing guide
nodes.rationale: Parlour started as one person's house made general; the most helpful contributions make it work in somebody else's house: a provider for a different engine, an integration for a different platform, Linux. A new voice or STT engine is a self-contained afternoon.

nodes.label: Development setup (Node 22, pnpm 10, Rust, parlour-dev)
nodes.rationale: The CLI runs straight from source with type stripping via packages/parlour/bin/parlour-dev, so there is no build step while working. pnpm -C packages/parlour build compiles to dist/, which is what npm publish ships and node dist/cli/main.js runs. The app is opened with pnpm -C apps/desktop app and drives whichever parlour its Settings tab points at (global install by default); set 'The parlour command' to the absolute path of parlour-dev to run the checkout.

nodes.label: PARLOUR_HOME scratch install and --no-service
nodes.rationale: PARLOUR_HOME keeps an experiment's config and secrets away from the real ones, but LaunchAgents are one per user, not per home: io.parlour.agent and io.parlour.whisper would be replaced by ones starting the checkout against the scratch directory, which is why init is run with --no-service. PARLOUR_SKIP_MODELS=1 skips the gigabyte of models. Recovery: parlour service uninstall then parlour init from the real install.

nodes.label: Where things go (change to location map)
nodes.rationale: New engine for an existing port: packages/parlour/src/providers/<kind>/<name>.ts registered in providers/index.ts, or an npm package. New tool source: src/integrations/<name>/. New port: core/ports.ts, a slot in core/config.ts, wiring in core/agent.ts, a fake in testing/; open an issue first because a port is a promise to every provider. Linux: a systemd service provider and non-avfoundation audio providers; core/paths.ts already follows XDG. CLI command: src/cli/<name>.ts exporting a Command, listed in cli/main.ts. The app (apps/desktop) drives the CLI, so add CLI capability first. The website is apps/site, one HTML file and one stylesheet.

nodes.label: Coding conventions (strict TS, .ts imports, node:test, Biome, British English)
nodes.rationale: TypeScript strict; relative imports inside packages/parlour/src use the .ts extension. Tests next to the source as *.test.ts with node:test and node:assert/strict, no test framework. Biome formats and lints. British English with no em dashes in comments, docs and CLI output; comments explain why, not what. Nothing secret in config: tokens come from secrets.env or the environment, never config.json, and are never printed.

nodes.label: Node type stripping constraint (no enums, parameter properties or decorators)
nodes.rationale: The source runs under Node's type stripping, which erases types and nothing else, so TypeScript features that emit runtime code (enums, parameter properties, decorators) are banned.

nodes.label: Doctor checks instead of unit tests for hardware/model/network providers
nodes.rationale: Providers that need hardware, a model or a network are not unit tested; each has a doctor() instead, and that is the part worth getting right. If the doctor cannot see it, it will break silently: a provider that depends on a binary, a file or a port checks for it in doctor() and says what to do about it.

nodes.label: Pull request conventions
nodes.rationale: One change per PR; say what it does and why; mention what could not be tested (e.g. a Linux change from a Mac). CI runs typecheck, lint, tests, build and cargo check and must be green. Commit messages are a sentence in the imperative.

nodes.label: Releasing (version:set, hand-written CHANGELOG, vX.Y.Z tag)
nodes.rationale: pnpm version:set X.Y.Z bumps both packages and the app; CHANGELOG.md is written by hand; pushing a vX.Y.Z tag publishes the package to npm and attaches the dmg to a GitHub release.
